newsitem.title: CHILE: GEPHARDT OFFERS HEDGED CHILE TRADE DEAL SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: GEPHARDT OFFERS HEDGED CHILE TRADE DEAL SUPPORT.

text.p: U.S. House of Representatives minority leader Richard Gephardt on Wednesday offered some encouragement for Chile's bid to join the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).

However, the Missouri Democrat quickly added that such a deal would have to grant environmental and labor interests the same sort of protection afforded to investments under international trade treaties.

Gephardt spoke briefly to reporters at La Moneda presidential palace after meeting Chilean President Eduardo Frei, whose government has been waiting since 1994 to become the fourth member of NAFTA, an agreement that groups the United States, Canada and Mexico.

"I think all of us hope that we can have a free trade agreement with Chile, but we need to address -- and we did speak about this (with Frei) -- the issues of labor and the environment being included in such a treaty," he said.
"My hope is that we can find a way to do it that is good for both countries," added Gephardt, who was an outspoken opponent of NAFTA before it was approved by the U.S. Congress in 1993.

He argued that the trade pacts the United States has with other countries have provisions covering intellectual property and capital. "What many of us seek is to have similar protection for labor and the environment," he said.
Asked about whether he would support President Bill Clinton's request for "fast track" authority to negotiate new trade deals, Gephardt answered only: "We'll see."
The White House is expected to kick off next month a campaign to obtain that authority from the Republican-controlled Congress.

Gephardt arrived here on Wednesday as part of a South American trip including stops in Venezuela, Brazil and Argentina. He is due to meet several Chilean cabinet members and business leaders on Thursday.
